subject: Morningside private cluster – sudden throughput regression and elevated 5xx rate
messages:
From: Chris D'Souza <chris@morning-side.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: eng@morning-side.com
Date: 2027-06-20 09:12 PDT
Subject: Sudden regression — 5xx spike and p95 jump on our on-prem cluster

Logan / Redwood team,

We started seeing a large increase in 5xx errors and p95 latency on our private cluster around 08:30 PT this morning after the small model patch you rolled last night. User-facing requests are timing out and the batch queue is piling up. Our SRE alerted and we've attached a short sample of error traces and metrics.

Key symptoms:
- P95 latency up from ~180ms to 1.9s for generate endpoints
- 5xx rate jumped to ~6% for a sustained 20 minutes then oscillating
- Throughput dropped ~25% despite similar incoming QPS

This is impacting scheduled clinical workflows. Can we get immediate help (root cause, rollback if needed, and an ETA)? We have a maintenance window this evening but need a mitigation sooner.

Attachments: error-samples.log

— Chris
Chris D'Souza
VP Engineering, Morningside Health
From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Chris D'Souza <chris@morning-side.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20 09:28 PDT
Subject: Re: Sudden regression — 5xx spike and p95 jump on our on-prem cluster

Chris — thanks for flagging this and for the logs. Sorry for the disruption. We're on it.

Immediate plan:
- Vivek (SRE) will triage the private cluster snapshot and attach initial findings here within 30–45 minutes.
- Monica will coordinate status/exec communications with your ops team.
- If the model patch is the culprit we can rollback the patch and route traffic to the previous model variant within 15 minutes of confirmation.

Questions for you (quick):
1) Can you confirm whether the private cluster has any backup capacity pool (burst nodes) currently enabled?
2) Do you have short-term permission for Redwood on-call to SSH into the metrics collector for a 15-min investigation?

I'm looping in Vivek and Monica. We'll send a concise triage note as soon as we have it.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: logan.wright@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: chris@morning-side.com, eng@morning-side.com
Date: 2027-06-20 10:02 PDT
Subject: RE: Sudden regression — 5xx spike and p95 jump on our on-prem cluster

Quick triage (initial):
- Observed KV cache churn and increased GPU memory fragmentation on the primary nodes starting 08:27 PT; fragmentation correlates with the model variant roll-forward at 01:12 UTC (last night).
- Inference kernel traces show several fallback code-paths where quantized kernels are failing to acquire expected workspace sizes; runtime falls back to slower FP kernels leading to extended latencies and periodic OOMs (these appear as downstream 5xx).
- Traffic profile: request size distribution unchanged, but a small subset of long-sequence requests (rare) is holding KV cache entries and blocking efficient batching.

Short-term mitigations (we can do now):
1) Disable quantized kernel path for the new variant (fast rollback of runtime flag) — expected p95 improvement in 5–10 minutes.
2) Enable a temporary burst pool (we'll spin 2 warm nodes) to absorb queue while we validate rollback.
3) Clear prefix cache entries for the identified client sessions (we will coordinate with your eng team to target IDs) — reduces KV pressure.

I'll attach a snapshot and CPU/GPU metrics in the Drive link. I recommend we avoid a full rollback unless the above fails; but we will proceed to full model rollback within 30 minutes if necessary.

Attachments: triage-snapshot.png

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Chris D'Souza <chris@morning-side.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20 11:05 PDT
Subject: Re: Sudden regression — action plan, exec brief and next steps

Chris — follow-up and consolidated plan after initial triage:

Summary:
- Cause: interaction between the new model variant's quantized kernel behavior and KV cache retention on long-sequence requests. This causes kernel fallbacks and periodic OOMs that manifest as 5xx and higher p95.
- Impact: intermittent 5xx spikes and sustained p95 degradation affecting clinical workflows.

Immediate actions we have initiated (underway):
- Disabled quantized kernel path for the new variant (rolled at 11:00 PT).
- Spun 2 warm burst nodes in your private pool to absorb queue.
- Cleared targeted KV cache entries for the affected sessions (coordination with your eng team).

Expected outcome: measurable p95 reduction within 10–15 minutes; 5xx rate should fall to baseline if mitigations work. If not, we will perform a full model rollback (previous stable variant) and keep burst nodes active until the evening maintenance window.

Next steps and responsibilities:
- Redwood (Vivek) will monitor metrics and post minute-by-minute updates in the Drive link.
- Redwood (Monica) will provide a timeline to Morningside execs and coordinate any contract/credits ask if required.
- Morningside to confirm whether we should proceed to a full rollback after 30 minutes if p95/5xx do not improve.

Escalation: I've copied Markus (Head of Product Ops) and Hannah (Customer Success lead) given potential impact to SLA. Markus, Hannah — quick heads-up in case Morningside requests an SLA credit or an extended on-site engagement.

I'll update in the thread as we see metric trends. Thanks for patience — we're treating this as high priority.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
